info.title: Snipe-IT laptop loans
info.description: Request contract for the fields used by the campus laptop loan tests (checkout of one laptop to one student user, and check-in of that same asset). Pinned to Snipe-IT v8.8.4, upstream commit 60fe07468534a283a473dbfe88244896b44c81bc. Observed on the running pinned build: every rejection that reaches the controller or the validator (field validation, unavailable asset, nonexistent asset, repeated check-in) is HTTP 200 with JSON status 'error'; only a missing permission is HTTP 403 and a missing or invalid token is HTTP 401. Clients must therefore assert the body status as well as the HTTP code. Vendor extensions: x-requirement and x-risk link a field to the team traceability IDs, x-valid-example names a runtime fixture (@student, @deployable_status, @location, @due_date, @today, @asset) or a literal, x-reference marks an integer that is a key into another table (boundary neighbours are checked against whether the row exists), x-boundary-note records why a field has no ordered boundary, x-server-note records what the pinned source actually enforces.

assetId.name: asset_id
assetId.x-boundary-note: The id is a database key with no maximum. Only the lower bound (0 and below is never a valid key) is a meaningful boundary; ids 1 and 2 depend on which rows exist, so the valid case uses the dedicated fixture asset instead.

workflowResult.description: Operation result. Inspect the status to distinguish success from a rejected action.

messages.description: Human-readable message (string) or a map of field names to message lists on validation errors.

post.x-server-note: Source: app/Http/Controllers/Api/AssetsController.php::checkout, app/Http/Requests/AssetCheckoutRequest.php, app/Models/Asset.php::availableForCheckout. checkout_to_type is inferred from the single filled assigned_* field when omitted, but the team contract always sends it. Observed: validation failures, unavailable assets, a nonexistent asset or target and a lost lock race all return HTTP 200 with status 'error'. An unknown user id yields the untranslated message key 'validation.exists_undeleted'.

checkout_to_type.x-server-note: The server also accepts 'asset' and 'location'; those targets are outside the project scope and are not generated.

assigned_user.x-server-note: numeric|exists_undeleted:users,id. A well-formed id that matches no live user is rejected with 422.

expected_checkin.x-boundary-note: A calendar date has no ordered numeric bound the server enforces (no minimum or maximum date rule). Equivalence partitions are used instead: valid date, impossible calendar date, wrong format, wrong type.
expected_checkin.x-server-note: Rule is 'nullable|date' (any string PHP can parse), so the server accepts more than the strict YYYY-MM-DD form used by the team.

checkout_at.x-boundary-note: Same as expected_checkin: no enforced ordered date bound.

name.x-server-note: Asset::rules name => nullable|max:255. A rejected name must leave the asset untouched. The database column was 191 characters at the pinned commit; branch sqe/asset-name-boundary widens it.

note.x-boundary-note: Free text with no length limit in the request rules, so no boundary. When the require_checkinout_notes setting is on, the field becomes required; that setting is exercised only in the isolated browser fixture.

status_id.x-server-note: nullable|exists:status_labels,id,deployable,1: only a deployable status label may be set during checkout.

requestable.x-boundary-note: Boolean has no ordered range; both values are one partition each.

200.description: Success or rejection; read the body status. Includes validation failures (messages is a map of field to messages), a nonexistent asset ('Asset not found') and an unavailable or already-returned asset.

403.description: Account lacks checkout/check-in permission (verified for the read-only reviewer).

post.x-server-note: Source: AssetsController::checkin. Unlike checkout this action has no FormRequest, so it performs no field validation of its own beyond what Asset::save() enforces. An empty body on an unassigned asset is rejected as already checked in (HTTP 200, status 'error'); a body that carries name, status_id, location_id or clear_name is applied as a metadata update without a second return.

status_id.x-server-note: No validation rule exists for status_id on this endpoint; the value is copied to the asset when filled.

clear_name.x-boundary-note: Single-value enumeration: only '1' triggers the clear; there is no ordered boundary.

note.x-boundary-note: Free text with no length limit in the request.

checkin_at.x-boundary-note: No enforced ordered date bound; the controller concatenates the value with the current time of day.

200.description: Success or rejection; read the body status. Includes validation failures (messages is a map of field to messages), a nonexistent asset ('Asset not found') and an unavailable or already-returned asset.

403.description: Account lacks checkout/check-in permission (verified for the read-only reviewer).

get.x-server-note: Read-back used after every operation. Fields asserted: assigned_to.id, expected_checkin.date, status.id, status.status_meta, name, checkout_counter, checkin_counter, last_checkout, last_checkin. Loan history is read from GET /reports/activity with item_type=asset.
